checkpoints.note: The saved run log prints `SOME/IP-SD Layer, 0 entries, 1 options` before the crash, confirming that the malformed payload passed format dispatch and layer construction.

The libFuzzer entry and pcap-reading harness only deliver the pcap bytes into project parsers. This helper is the first project statement that turns attacker bytes into the internal entries-length state used on the vulnerable path.

For the witness, `lenEntries == 8` and the options-length field is `00 00 00 20`, so this check admits a layer that is 27 bytes shorter than its declared entries-plus-options extent. The patch fixes this exact obligation by checking the full entries-plus-options size and by validating option boundaries with `countOptions(count, data)` before accepting the layer.

The crashing load is not the first constructor at offset 24. It is the second one at offset 40, whose `majorVersion_ttl` field sits at layer bytes 48-51 / raw packet bytes 76-79, so the 4-byte read starts 7 bytes past the 69-byte packet buffer exactly as AddressSanitizer reports.
